prompt:
Create a high-fidelity desktop website comp for the public home of Protocolo Lupita, a Mexican public-interest prototype that helps people review suspicious messages and receive safe next steps. Wide landscape 16:10 browser viewport, composed as a real webpage screenshot, not a poster.

WORLD: civic wayfinding signs and public-service directories, translated into a precise digital service. Use only the pinned palette: deep navy #10213F, warm off-white #F3F0E6, and restrained gold #D5A928. Gold marks route direction and active navigation; use crisp lines, broad calm surfaces, and clear destination labels. The supplied fox-shield logo is the exact brand asset: place it in the upper-left header, preserving its proportions and colors unchanged. No gradients, no generic equal-sized icon-card grid, no stock photography, no decorative city landmarks, no map claiming real activity.

COMPOSITION: short navy header with shield, “Protocolo Lupita”, and concise public links. A broad warm off-white hero features the existing citizen question “¿Recibiste un mensaje o una llamada sospechosa?” in large, clean Spanish typography. Supporting copy invites the visitor to review a message or learn what to do next. Place a dominant gold route plaque with navy text, “Revisar un SMS”, and a secondary outlined route, “Hacer un reporte”. Beside the question, draw one simple, functional directional route line that branches to three clearly labeled destinations: “Revisar SMS”, “Reportar”, and “Consultar avisos”. Keep the line and plaque system architectural and legible, with no false street map. Separate the government entrance as a smaller, clearly labeled route, not a competing action. Include an honest note that this is a local demonstration with fictional data.

Render clear accurate Spanish text, sharp alignment, spacious margins, confident hierarchy, and visible content through most of the first screen. The surface should look like public-service navigation, not generic cyber marketing.
